# Continual ARC Puzzle Solving

Use for sequential ARC-style puzzles with demos, limited submissions and strict action schema.

## Operating loop
1. Parse task, budgets, dimensions and action contract. For JSON-only turns, emit exactly one valid action object.
2. Inventory background, components, shapes, locations, markers and alignments.
3. Separate evidence from hypotheses. Compare input/output cellwise; explain changes AND invariants.
4. Spend demos only to distinguish explicit candidate rules. Incorporate each returned pair before another action.
5. Validate any rule against all demos, including unchanged candidates; apply mechanically and verify grid dimensions/cell values.
6. After incorrect feedback, discard the tested hypothesis rather than slightly varying it.

## task-4c372242: variable leading-trim recurrence (confirmed across fresh instances)

Do not assume a single crop rule from the task ID. A previously validated variant crops only the maximal prefix of all-background rows, preserving width and all remaining rows. In the latest instance, that rule produced a wrong no-op; live demo then revealed the correct transform: remove the maximal prefix of all-background rows **and** the maximal prefix of all-background columns, cropping the top and left only. Preserve all remaining cells in their original order, including trailing blank rows/columns. Demo (15x20, bg5): the first row was entirely background and was removed; no leading column was entirely background, so columns remained. Test (11x20, bg5): first column was entirely background, but row 0 was not; accepted output removed only column 0, yielding 11x19. Thus inspect both edges from current input and use current demos to choose the variant; never infer solely from task ID. The initial accepted-looking row-only hypothesis was rejected on this test.

## task-4c372242: latest demonstrated recurrence — crop top row unconditionally

Fresh instance (test 16x16, background 4) solved on first submission after Demo 1. Demo input was 10x27 with a mixed first row: first row had 8s at columns 4-10 and 14, and 3s elsewhere. Output replaced the entire first row with background 3, while every original row 0-8 moved down unchanged to rows 1-9; dimensions stayed 10x27 and the original last row was dropped. In other words, shift the whole grid down by one row, insert a blank/background row at top, discard the bottom row. The test had background 4 and was transformed by inserting an all-4 first row, shifting input rows 0-14 to output rows 1-15, and dropping original row 15. Accepted on first try.

This is distinct from all crop-only, leading-blank trim, and selected-first-row shift variants below. The only fresh demo establishes unconditional one-row downward shift with background fill at top and fixed dimensions. On future recurrence, inspect fresh pair for exact direction and background; do not infer from task ID alone.

## task-4c372242: crop leading all-background rows only (validated recurrence)

Transformation: remove the maximal prefix of rows that are entirely the background color, shifting all remaining rows upward unchanged; keep the original width and all trailing rows, even if blank. Do not remove leading all-background columns. Background color varies by instance.

Evidence in current run: Demo 1 (24x4, background 4, foreground 2) had rows 0-3 entirely background; output removed exactly original row 0, leaving 23 rows. Demo 2 (10x19, background 6, foreground 1) had row 0 all-background; output removed exactly that one row. Demo 3 (3x7, background 9) had no all-background leading row because row 0/1 were background but row 2 contained 6s; output unchanged. Demo 5 (23x12, bg6, fg9) removed rows 0-4, the five-row all-background prefix, retaining all subsequent rows including trailing blank rows. Demo 6 (28x4, bg3/9) removed no rows because row 0 contains foreground 9. Demo 7 (20x16, bg0, fg2) removed rows 0-4, the maximal blank prefix, retaining shape and remainder. Demo 8 (13x18, bg8, fg2) removed rows 0-3, exactly the top blank prefix.

Test (19x28) began with one all-background row 0; accepted output was rows 1-18 of the input, yielding 18x28. Earlier wrong submissions were no-op (attempt 1), then malformed/incorrectly shifted versions that retained the first row or duplicated variants. Make a mechanical check: locate the first row containing any non-background cell, output from there through the original final row, unchanged.

## task-4c372242: shift first active row down one (freshly confirmed variant)

In a fresh instance with background 5, test was 6x17. Rows 0-1 were all background; rows 2-3 contained a vertical pair of color-4 cells at column 3; rows 4-5 were all background. Demo 1 (17x10, background 8) had color-0 cells at (5,1) and (6,2); output blanked row 5 and moved that pair down one to (6,1) and (7,2), preserving all other rows and dimensions. Keep width and height fixed. Applied to test: first active row 2 is blanked, original row2 marker moves to row3 and original row3 marker moves to row4; accepted.
